# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — six scorer-grounded prompt fixes across all 6 failing + 2 flaky traces
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file + cluster):
  - task_template.md — turned the per-round "verify" step into an ORDERED precondition
    checklist (print value+type for answer_position; no empty/0-default cells; numbers/dates
    typed; baseline+row-count sanity; never resubmit identical code). Cluster: cosmetic-verify
    + wasted-rounds (47766, 52216, 250-20, 493-18, 54638).
  - task_template.md — added the exact ```python fence worked example, banned
    `<tool_call>`/XML/`call:` wrappers, and gave the recovery ("re-send same code fenced").
    Cluster: no-output/malformed-fence (48365).
  - prompt.md — "edit in place with openpyxl; don't round-trip a whole sheet via pandas; if you
    must, use header=None/header=False; read ID/code columns dtype=str." Cluster: pandas
    round-trip corruption (493-18, 250-20, 262-17).
  - prompt.md — "write dates/times as real datetime/time values, never strftime/str/TEXT."
    Cluster: date/time-as-string (32438).
  - prompt.md — "no sheet in answer_position ⇒ first sheet; named sheet ⇒ that exact sheet."
    Cluster: wrong-sheet (54638).
  - prompt.md — "use a stable sort (kind='mergesort')." Cluster: unstable sort (262-17).
  - prompt.md — "delete rows ⇒ remove and shift up"; "re-derive a key from the data when a
    lookup/filter collapses to empty/0" (the wrong-guess half of 47766 & 52216).
- Expected effect + why safe: each edit targets a trace-confirmed failure and is additive/
  conditional. Grounded in the real scorer (evaluation.py): numbers coerce to float @2dp (so
  number-as-text already matches — deliberately NOT touched), a real time is compared trimmed
  to HH:MM (so 32438's literal string fails), a no-`!` range defaults to sheetnames[0]. Passing
  32902 (openpyxl, numbers) and 48745 (pandas header=None, text labels) are each checked
  against all six edits: none changes their action (the pandas safeguard literally names
  48745's path; the date/number scoping excludes both; neither sorts; both already on the first
  sheet and already verify with all cells filled).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed iteration, LEDGER/JOURNAL/rejected.jsonl all empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet. Explicitly did NOT add a blanket "numbers must be numeric not
  string" rule because the scorer coerces numeric strings to float, so it would be a no-op that
  risks over-coercing 48745's text output.
- High-value clusters still not fully cracked: 250-20's groupby over-merge is a logic ambiguity
  (its real dedup key is narrower than bare B&C) — only nudged via the verify row-count check,
  not solved; a future iteration may need a worked dedup example if it stays flaky.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is rejected as net-zero, the most likely
  culprit is the openpyxl-in-place steer perturbing 48745 — in that case keep edits E1/E3/E4/E5/
  E6 and drop/rescope E2 (the pandas steer) rather than abandon the cluster.
- Focus next iteration: confirm which edits moved which tasks from the RESULT stamp; if 250-20
  stays flaky, add a worked remove-duplicate-rows example; re-check whether the verify checklist
  needs to be shorter for the weaker reader.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.533 Δ=+0.200 · fixed={32438, 52216} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
